meta.description: Real-time AI-powered security extension for modern web browsing

title.line1: That sketchy link in your email?

hero.subtitle: Hover over links to see if they're trying to steal your stuff. Red = bad, green = fine. Built this because I got tired of my mom falling for phishing emails.

cta.helperText: Free • Chrome only • Made by humans

problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: Why traditional browser security falls short
content: Most browser protection relies on blocklists. They work only after a threat has already been reported.
Modern phishing attacks change domains, designs, and behavior constantly — which is why many scams slip through undetected.

solution.label: Our Solution
solution.title: A more reliable approach
content: BrowseSight focuses on intent. It examines how a page behaves, what it asks for, and how it tries to influence the user.
This allows it to flag suspicious pages even when they are new, unreported, or carefully disguised.

items.title: Advanced phishing detection
items.description: Detects credential harvesting pages, fake login forms, and sophisticated social engineering attacks using behavioral analysis.

items.title: Brand impersonation alerts
items.description: Identifies typosquatting, lookalike domains, and visual impersonation attempts targeting trusted brands and services.

items.title: URL unshortening
items.description: Automatically reveals the true destination of shortened links from bit.ly, t.co, and other URL shorteners before you click.

items.title: Pressure tactic detection
items.description: Flags urgency manipulation like countdown timers, limited-time offers, and high-pressure sales tactics commonly used in scams.

items.title: Form security analysis
items.description: Warns when sensitive data is requested on insecure pages and identifies the purpose of forms (login, payment, etc.).

items.title: AI threat intelligence
items.description: Leverages multiple security APIs and AI analysis to provide human-readable explanations of detected threats.

steps.title: Signal collection
steps.description: When a page loads or a link is hovered, BrowseSight collects visible signals such as the URL, page text, form elements, and redirect behavior.

steps.title: Local evaluation
steps.description: Trusted domains and cached results are checked first to avoid unnecessary processing.

steps.title: Risk analysis
steps.description: Unknown pages are evaluated across multiple risk factors including brand impersonation, urgency tactics, and unsafe data collection.

steps.title: Score calculation
steps.description: Each risk factor contributes to a final safety score that reflects the overall trust level of the page.

steps.title: User feedback
steps.description: A clear visual indicator and explanation are shown to help the user understand the assessment.

usage.label: Getting Started
usage.title: Using BrowseSight

steps.title: Download the extension
steps.description: Download the official BrowseSight extension package from the provided source.

steps.title: Open Chrome Extensions
steps.description: Navigate to chrome://extensions in your Chrome browser.

steps.title: Enable Developer Mode
steps.description: Turn on Developer Mode using the toggle in the top-right corner of the page.

steps.title: Load BrowseSight
steps.description: Click 'Load unpacked' and select the extracted BrowseSight folder.

usage.note: BrowseSight does not require account creation, sign-in, or initial configuration.

sections.heading: Use of BrowseSight
sections.content: BrowseSight is provided as a security assistance tool. While it aims to reduce risk, it does not guarantee protection from all threats.

sections.heading: Data handling
sections.content: BrowseSight processes website content strictly for security analysis. No personal browsing data is sold or used for advertising.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
sections.content: BrowseSight is provided on an as-is basis. Users remain responsible for their browsing decisions.

installation.context: BrowseSight is currently distributed as an unpacked Chrome extension to maintain transparency during development.

steps.title: Open Chrome Extensions
steps.description: Navigate to chrome://extensions in your Chrome browser.

steps.title: Enable Developer Mode
steps.description: Turn on Developer Mode using the toggle in the top-right corner of the Extensions page.

steps.title: Load the extension
steps.description: Click 'Load unpacked' and select the BrowseSight folder containing the extension files.

steps.title: Confirm installation
steps.description: BrowseSight will appear in the extensions list and activate immediately.

installation.note: No account creation, sign-in, or initial configuration is required.

whatIsInstalled.description: BrowseSight uses standard Chrome extension components that are fully inspectable.

components.name: manifest.json
components.purpose: Defines permissions, extension behavior, and Chrome compatibility.

components.name: content scripts
components.purpose: Analyze visible webpage signals such as text, forms, and structure.

components.name: background service worker
components.purpose: Handles security logic and communication with the backend API.

components.name: popup interface
components.purpose: Displays safety results, explanations, and extension status.

whatIsInstalled.statement: No hidden binaries or executables are included. All files are readable and inspectable.

permissions.chromeMessage: No access needed. These extensions don't need to see and change information on this site.
explanation: BrowseSight does not request blanket access to all websites.
It does not modify page content.
It does not read personal data.
permissions.principle: Permissions are requested only when required for security analysis.

usage.intro: BrowseSight is designed to work quietly in the background without interrupting normal browsing.
behavior: Links and pages are analyzed automatically when hovered or visited.
You are notified only when something requires attention.

indicators.description: No suspicious behavior detected. The page appears legitimate.
Some risk signals detected. Proceed carefully.
Strong indicators of phishing, impersonation, or malicious intent detected.

usage.controlStatement: BrowseSight provides information and context. The final decision always remains with the user.
